The S&P 500 slipped 0.30% to 7,720.39, the Dow dipped 0.25% to 52,342.56, while the VIX rose 1.71% to 17.20. Small caps bucked the trend, with the Russell 2000 gaining 1.01%. Healthcare and real estate sectors rose 2.40% and 2.21% respectively, while info tech and communication services fell 1.18% and 1.87%.

Among megacaps, Meta rose 1.96% and Apple 1.48%, while Amazon fell 4.25% and Alphabet A dropped 12.64%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 1.42%, ending a four-day rally, with Intel down 3.62% and memory stocks broadly lower. The Nasdaq Golden Dragon China Index rose 0.20%.

Amazon reported Q3 net sales of $201.94 billion, up 12% but slightly below expectations, with EPS of $1.89. AWS revenue grew 39.3% to $45.98 billion, beating estimates, though online stores grew just 2%. Capital expenditures hit $77.26 billion, and trailing 12-month free cash flow turned negative at $42.36 billion. The company maintained its ~$220 billion capex plan and guided Q4 sales of $240-247 billion, sending shares down over 10% after hours.

Intel posted Q3 revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21%, with adjusted EPS of $0.52 beating estimates. However, Q4 guidance of $15-16 billion revenue and $0.25 EPS fell well short of expectations, sending shares down over 20% after hours. Data center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3 billion, while client revenue fell 5%. It has cut its Q4 net marketable borrowing estimate from $628 billion to $618 billion, about 1.6%. Treasury started the quarter with $34 billion more cash than it assumed in August and still expects to end the year with $850 billion. Without that extra starting cash, Treasury says it would expect to borrow $24 billion more than it projected in August.The first numbers to check are the 10- and 30-year auction sizes. If auction sizes are broadly in line and long yields fall, look for stronger spot demand for BTC.For bills, the source of the money matters. Just Now, Altman Reveals OpenAI's New Model: So Excited I Didn't Sleep for Two Nights | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsJust Now, Altman Reveals OpenA...Just Now, Altman Reveals OpenAI's New Model: So Excited I Didn't Sleep for Two NightsmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-30Last updated on 2026-10-30AbstractOpenAI CEO Sam Altman revealed on a podcast that an unreleased internal model, tested during a weekend experiment codenamed "Hold-my-beer," solved decades-old unsolved academic problems across multiple disciplines—including the Navier-Stokes equations—astonishing researchers and keeping Altman awake for two nights. He described the moment as a collective shock and a turning point: the era of humans laboring for years on hard problems is ending, and even top mathematicians risk becoming obsolete, like farm horses replaced by tractors.

Altman warned that AI will uncover far more severe security vulnerabilities than expected, and that sandboxes may not contain a model far smarter than any human researcher—suggesting the internet itself may need to be rebuilt with AI. He advocated many slightly-superhuman agents working as coordinated "teams" rather than one all-powerful model, enabled by test-time compute and chain-of-thought, with millions of dollars of compute now able to attack a single problem in parallel.

He predicted a "Macintosh moment" for personal agents that eliminate "fake work" like filling out web forms, and argued companies' real moat will be fulfillment capability, not UI code. On recursive self-improvement, he said AI will soon design better AI architectures, capturing even 5% efficiency gains as major breakthroughs.
